name: /wtft
tagline: Where The F***ing Tokens?! (WTFT) - Cost Auditing Widget
description: Displays a horizontal TUI bar chart of your session's cost, one row per bin, split by category (Spec, Code, Plan, Agents, ...). Each turn's cost goes to its category and includes the context re-send overhead, and Prompt means pure conversational replies. Cumulative mode (the default) stacks each category's running sum, its earlier bins as █ and this bin's share as ✨. Bucket mode (-b) is a scatter: each category's own cost in the bin is one cell at its place on the scale, and the larger cost takes a shared cell. Under --tokens the bar counts tokens and is stacked in both modes. Each row also prints four numbers: incremental cost, running total cost, incremental tokens and running total tokens. --cost and --tokens choose the bar, not those numbers. When the label area (time label and numbers) is wider than a quarter of the width, it compacts in five steps, each keeping the ones before: one-space gaps, whole numbers ($487, 590k), no + sign, no currency sign on the incremental cost, t in place of tok. If the bar is then under 15 cells, the token numbers drop, then the cost numbers. In the Pi widget a /wtft call saves the interval, limit, mode and timezone flags it is given to the wtft config, which the CLI also reads for its defaults, and creates that config if there is none; a call carrying -F, -o, -p, -H, an emoji flag, or --tokens after any --cost saves none of them. Exit codes are the CLI's: /wtft answers in Pi notifications and has none. Either surface refuses a call with an argument it does not recognise, a flag with no value, or a value a flag cannot use, and does nothing else, --help and --json included: the CLI says why on stderr and exits 2, /wtft in an error notification. Of the report flags that take a value, only --interval, --limit, --width, --tz and --timezone also take it as --flag=value.

why.scenario: You just finished a coding session and want to see where your token costs went — was it all spec-writing or code refactoring?
why.result: A bar chart of your cost by activity (Spec, Code, Plan, Agents, ...) in 1-hour bins, so you see which hours cost the most. The demo is the CLI's report; the Pi widget draws its chart without the session path line or the padding rows.
demo: [90m  CH: 79% cache hit (2.7M read / 3.5M total ops)[0m

why.scenario: You're tracking costs over a full workday and want finer granularity.
why.result: Up to the last 12 four-hour bins that hold turns are displayed: several days at a glance, six bins to a day. The CLI pads the chart to 12 rows; the Pi widget is not padded and shows as many as fit its 10 lines.
demo: [90m  CH: 79% cache hit (2.7M read / 3.5M total ops)[0m

why.scenario: You're auditing Claude Code sessions (not Pi) to compare costs across harnesses.
why.result: The chart pulls session data from your Claude Code session directory instead of Pi's, rendering the same bar chart for Claude interactions. (CLI only — /wtft always reports the Pi session it runs in.)
demo: [90m  CH: 79% cache hit (2.7M read / 3.5M total ops)[0m

why.scenario: You're standing in a git worktree (or the main clone) with more than one session logged there in the last 20 minutes, and want to pick which one to look at.
why.result: The session picker (#89) opens, scoped by default to THIS directory alone and to the last 20 minutes — folder-name matching, no whole-repo scan. Ctrl+W widens to every checkout of the current repo (worktree rows compact to <repo>/w/<branch>); Ctrl+A widens to every project on the machine; Ctrl+B narrows to the checkout of your current git branch; Ctrl+T cycles the time window (20m -> 1h -> 1d -> 1w -> all -> 20m). Outside a git repo, Ctrl+W has nothing to widen into. Use --dir <path> to anchor the picker somewhere other than the current directory. CLI only — /wtft always reports the Pi session it runs in.
demo: 💸 WTFT — select session log (j/k navigate, Enter select, q quit · Ctrl+A/Tab all · Ctrl+W worktrees · Ctrl+B branch · Ctrl+T window)

why.scenario: You want to scroll through a long cost history that doesn't fit in the TUI widget.
why.result: A fullscreen scrollable pager overlay opens with the expanded cost timeline. (Pi TUI only — not available in the CLI.)

why.scenario: The 'Other' category in your WTFT widget is consuming a large share of your session cost and you want to drill into which specific commands are causing it.
why.result: A grouped histogram appears, breaking 'Other' commands into semantic sub-categories (Build & Bundling, Linting & Formatting, System Utilities, etc.) with per-command counts and costs. Unclassified commands appear under their own section.

why.scenario: You're running Claude Code and want a companion terminal showing live token costs as your session progresses.
why.result: A real-time updating bar chart renders in-place as new interactions are logged. Runs until Ctrl+C or 'q'. Scrollback above the chart is preserved. Ideal in a separate tmux pane. CLI only — the Pi widget ignores --watch.

why.scenario: A script or another agent needs this session's exact cost as data, not as a picture.
why.result: One JSON object on stdout (schema wtft/session@8): exact totals, per-model and per-category rows, the uncounted blind spot, the spawn tree and the provisional verdict, which exit 9 repeats. No ANSI on stdout; prose goes to stderr. With no interactive terminal, name the session with -s. CLI only — the Pi widget ignores --json. Contract: docs/spec-26-json.md.

why.scenario: Your launcher starts whole agent sessions (a review lens, a herdr child) and you want their cost counted under the session that started them.
why.result: One parent->child edge is appended to the spawn ledger. The --json and --tokens reports then count the child under spawned and tree, while total keeps meaning this session's own turns. Record it at spawn time: neither transcript names the other, so no later parse can find the edge. CLI only — /wtft has no spawn-record.

why.scenario: You want to see the exact USD amount on your billing invoice or reconcile costs across multiple providers.
why.result: WTFT uses public pricing estimates per model and excludes things like caching discounts, free-tier credits, or provider-specific billing nuances. It's a directional cost-awareness tool — not an accounting ledger.

why.scenario: Your harness's own cost counter reads higher than WTFT's TOTAL and you want to know whether WTFT is miscounting or just can't see something.
why.result: TOTAL is strictly derived from recorded usage — every dollar traces to a `usage` object in the transcript. Below it, an UNCOUNTED line names the events the harness bills for but writes no usage for: /compact requests and 'while you were away' recaps, counted across the session and every subagent transcript. They are deliberately NOT priced and NOT in TOTAL. Measured across seven logged Claude Code sessions, this blind spot was 4.72% of the harness's own counter. The line appears only when a count is non-zero, and only in the CLI's non-watch --tokens path — --watch does not render it yet, and /wtft --tokens never does.
demo: Model           Input     Output  Reasoning Cache-Read Cache-Write       Cost
UNCOUNTED  3 recaps — billed by the harness; the transcript records
no usage for them, so they are NOT in TOTAL above (#149)

why.scenario: Your session has been idle for a while and the model cache has expired, or you're running a local model like Ollama with no remote caching at all.
why.result: The Pi widget's daemon status text, under the chart's legend, says which: 'idle (cache expires in Nmin)' while the model's prompt cache lasts, 'idle (cache emptied)' once it has passed, and 'idle (local model)' for a model with no remote cache. A session with no turns to chart yet shows 'Cache Empty' (cloud models) or 'No Cache (local model)' in place of the chart, with the status text under it. Pi widget only — the CLI prints no daemon status.

usage.desc: Bin size: a whole count and a unit, m, h, d, w, or t for turns (also turn or turns), e.g. 7m, 4h, 1d, 1w, 5t; a w bin is one week whatever its count. Default: the wtft config's interval, else 1h. Any other value, a count of 0 included, is refused (exit 2). --interval=<value> also works.

The number of bin rows shown, newest first. Default: the wtft config's limit when it sets one, else 17 in the CLI and 10 in the Pi extension; --watch also takes a limit from a wtft-settings entry in the session log first. -l takes a whole number of 1 or more; any other value is refused (exit 2). A fractional or negative limit from the config or a session log is rounded down to a whole number, at least 1. The CLI chart, in a report and in --watch, always shows exactly that many rows: with fewer bins it is padded (to at most 1000 rows, and in --watch at most the terminal's height) with placeholder rows, a dash under each label column and an empty bar area. --watch drops placeholder rows first when the frame would not fit the terminal. The Pi widget is not padded, and shows fewer rows when the widget would pass Pi's 10-line cap. --limit=<value> also works.

CLI only. Specify an explicit session .jsonl file path, or a fuzzy substring filter (e.g. 'b04c'). When the argument is not an existing file, it filters discovered sessions by basename or path substring, searched over the PRE-#89 discovery population (#89) -- for Claude Code, every checkout of the current repo (fan-out) plus the #156 union arm, unbounded in time; for Pi with no --dir, every Pi session on the machine -- unlike a bare launch with no -s, which searches only the picker's own scoped, time-windowed population (this worktree, last 20 minutes, by default). An explicit ask for a known session is never narrowed by that browsing convenience window, but it is not literally "every session on the machine" for Claude Code. If exactly one match, runs immediately; with an interactive terminal and multiple matches, shows the session picker filtered to them; with an interactive terminal and ZERO matches, exits 1 with 'matches no discovered sessions'; with no interactive terminal, zero or several matches exit 10 (#89, see Exit codes) instead of prompting. An absolute .jsonl path that does not exist YET is accepted as a pending session (#308), reported at exit 0 rather than as an error -- or 9 when --tokens or --json finds a live descendant, or 1 when the log parser daemon exits before serving it (see Exit codes).

CLI only. Anchor directory for Claude Code session discovery (default: current directory). The flag picks the anchor, not the SCOPE: with no -s, the picker's own default scope (#89) folder-matches this ONE directory alone, no fan-out. Ctrl+W widens to every checkout of the anchor's repo (main clone plus every worktree), so sibling-worktree sessions are listed only on that keypress, or under the pre-#89 legacy discovery an explicit -s still searches (see -s's own entry). An anchor outside any git repo means exactly that directory even under Ctrl+W, so '--dir ~' still does not list every session on the machine. When the working directory has been deleted, wtft runs from this directory, which must then be an absolute path, or from the home directory and says so.

The Pi widget's width for that call, capped at 240 and at the terminal width; the widget's next refresh (a settled turn, or the 1-minute timer) sizes it to the terminal again. With no -w the widget sizes to the terminal, at most 240 columns. Pi extension only — the CLI parses the flag and ignores it, sizing output from the terminal width minus --pad. -w takes a whole number of 1 or more; any other value is refused (exit 2). --width=<value> also works.

Display timezone, an IANA name (e.g. America/New_York, Europe/London, Asia/Tokyo). Default: the wtft config's timezone; else system local in the CLI, and America/Los_Angeles in the Pi widget. --tz=<value> works too.

Render mode; the later flag wins. Cumulative: each bar is the running sum up to and including its bin. Bucket: each bar is its bin's own total, a scatter for cost and stacked for --tokens. Default: the wtft config's mode, else cumulative. The Pi widget saves a -c or -b it is given to the wtft config, which the CLI also reads, except on the calls the description lists as saving nothing (--tokens after any --cost among them).

Launch an interactive scrollable fullscreen pager overlay to view expanded cost history: up/down arrows or k/j scroll a line, PageUp/PageDown a page, q or Esc closes it. With no -l it holds up to 100 bins. It takes -i, -l, -b/-c and --tz for that view and saves none of them; -H in the same call hides the widget and opens no pager. Pi TUI only — the CLI refuses -p with exit 1 and suggests piping to a pager instead.

Print a histogram of 'Other' commands grouped by semantic sub-category (Build, Lint, Test, Text & File Processing, System, etc.) with per-command counts and costs. A token that is not a plausible command name is normalizer residue, not a program that ran: those are quarantined under [Parse miss] and carry a ##PARSE-MISS## marker so misses can be counted rather than mistaken for commands. Tokens come from commands the session ran, so they are control-character-stripped and length-capped before rendering. The CLI prints it under the chart; /wtft shows it alone, in a notification.

Show or hide the WTFT widget below the editor. Pi extension only; both are accepted and inert in the CLI. -H hides it until a /wtft call that draws it (plain, with chart settings, -S, --tokens or --cost) or a new Pi session; an emoji flag, -F, -o, -p, --help, --why and --version leave it hidden. -S does nothing of its own beyond being such a call, and --hide --show and --show --hide both hide it. -H is ignored in a call that also carries -F, an emoji flag, --version, --help, --why, -o, or --tokens as the later of --tokens and --cost: that flag runs instead, and --tokens draws the widget. With --cost as the later, the cost bar is saved and the widget then hidden.

Emoji in the chart on or off; the later flag wins, and --emojii and --no-emojii are aliases. Off, the chart draws single-width characters in their place. CLI, --watch included: for that run only, over the wtft config's disabledEmoji. Pi widget: saves the choice as the config's disabledEmoji, which the CLI also reads; the call's other flags are ignored but --no-cost and --no-tokens, and -F, which runs instead of it.
Watch a session file for changes and re-render the bar chart in real-time (companion terminal mode). q or Ctrl+C to exit. CLI only; the Pi widget ignores it.

CLI only; the Pi widget ignores it. List the log parser daemons and their leases: PID, RUNNING or DEAD (stale pid: gone, a zombie, or a live process that is not a log parser daemon), tagger version, idle age (0s until the session has been idle 2m2s; ? when unknown) and session. A harness's lease names the session that harness's .served hand-off lists for that lease; any other lease names its holder's --session, resolved against the holder's working directory. The tagger version is the first tag file found beside that session, not the running build's. A lease reading rebuild (left by -F or a failed tag write) is not listed; a lease with no such session shows (hash: <lease hash>), and a daemon holding no lease here shows v? and idle ?. Off Linux (no /proc) every live pid reads RUNNING, and daemons holding no lease here, a harness among them, are not listed.

CLI only; the Pi widget ignores it. Remove every lease whose holder is dead or not a log parser daemon (not counted in the total). Send SIGTERM, without waiting, to each per-session log parser daemon whose session is gone: its file is absent, it was not moved, and its tag holds a turn or a _meta record. One that refuses the signal (another user's, EPERM) keeps its lease. A harness daemon is not killed because the session it was started for is gone; it drops a gone session itself. A per-session fixture daemon, one whose --session or root environment (WTFT_CLAUDE_PROJECTS_DIR, WTFT_PI_SESSIONS_DIR) is under the tmp dir (os.tmpdir(): TMPDIR, TMP or TEMP, else /tmp), that holds no lease there is sent SIGTERM too. A harness daemon is never killed; it stops itself once it has served nothing, holds no idle-dropped session and retries no adoption for 24h.

CLI only; the Pi widget ignores it. Stop every log parser daemon that holds a lease or a harness root pid file under this temp dir, remove those files (except the lease a respawn claims), and spawn one fresh daemon per stopped holder with that process's own --session, root environment and XDG_STATE_HOME, claiming that session's lease for it at once when the lease is free (a harness daemon comes back for its root and takes its other sessions from the hand-off it wrote on stopping). A holder still running 2 s after SIGTERM is sent SIGKILL; one still running 2 s after that keeps its lease and is not respawned. A holder that refuses the signal (another user's, EPERM) keeps its lease or root pid file and is not respawned; so does a harness still running after SIGKILL. A holder that is not a live daemon only has its file removed; a live harness daemon holding a lease without --session is respawned with its own --harness. A respawn that neither runs nor hands off to a live holder within the settle wait is reported as failed; a failed respawn or a holder left running makes wtft-daemon exit 1. A harness daemon holding no lease is stopped and not respawned, and the next wtft starts it again, unless a respawn handed its session to it: that one is left running. On Linux: the liveness check and the --session read use /proc, so off Linux nothing is stopped or respawned and the files are removed while their daemons keep running.

CLI only; the Pi widget ignores it. Stop the log parser daemon for a specific session path; ~ and a relative path are resolved first. --stop with no session after it, or followed by an argument starting with -, is refused (exit 2). A harness session, found through the session's lease, is dropped from the shared process, which stays up; Linux only: both lookups read /proc, so off Linux --stop reports that no daemon was found and exits 0 while the session stays served. A per-session daemon holding a lease here is found by its own --session resolved against its working directory, so one that followed a moved session is found by its old path; it is sent SIGTERM and reported stopped without waiting. A daemon that refuses the signal (another user's, EPERM) keeps its lease, and the command exits 1.

Force a full re-parse of the session's tag from its transcript. On Linux, a session a harness log parser daemon serves is rebuilt by that daemon, which keeps serving its other sessions; the CLI's report waits for it to begin, and when the harness has not taken the session up within 10 s, the CLI says so and exits 1 with no report. Otherwise a running log parser daemon for the session is stopped and every version of its tag file deleted; when that daemon is still running 2 s later, or another daemon claimed its lease meanwhile (for a harness session: the lease changed or was removed before it could be marked rebuild), nothing is deleted and the CLI exits 1, as it does when the holder cannot be verified as a log parser daemon, the lease cannot be read, the rebuild lease cannot be written, the daemon cannot be signalled, or a lease or tag file cannot be deleted. In the Pi widget -F runs instead of the call's other flags and waits for no harness: a notification says what it did, or why nothing was rebuilt.

Target a specific harness for auto-discovery (pi, claude-code, or auto). Default: auto; any other value is refused (exit 2), so a harness added through ~/.config/wtft/harnesses.json is found by auto but cannot be named here. CLI only; the Pi widget ignores it.

Thinking token budget, a positive whole number, for utilization percentage display in --tokens output. CLI only; /wtft --tokens takes the budget from the thinking level last selected while Pi has been running, and shows no utilization while that level is off or before one is selected.

Emit one JSON object on stdout (schema wtft/session@8) instead of the chart: exact un-abbreviated totals, per-model rows with a 'priced' flag, per-category rows in a fixed order, the #149 uncounted blind spot, the #116 spawned lineage (with spawned.ledgerError saying the ledger could not be READ, which is not the same as nothing having spawned) plus a tree total, total.untaggedCostUsd sized from the same per-interaction figures the chart bins (#119, so total.costUsd + total.untaggedCostUsd equals the chart's own running total within float accumulation error), the #137 subagents[] rows naming one transcript each with the .meta.json the harness wrote beside it and, as total, what TOTAL already holds for that subagent (inside total, never to be added to it; null when nothing of it is tagged yet; absent on a stale-version tag, whose lines carry no source key) (meta is null when there is no such file, or when it cannot be read, which also adds a subagent-meta-unreadable notice naming it; a meta that reads but does not parse is null with no notice -- a Pi sibling has none and is still a real, LISTED subagent; being listed is not evidence its cost is in total, which is the tag file's business and independent of meta -- and the subagents key is OMITTED ENTIRELY, never [], when discovery could not complete), the provisional verdict as a field, and the session identity. total means THIS SESSION'S OWN TURNS; tree is total plus every RESOLVED launcher-spawned descendant the ledger records, each priced with the subagent and claude -p sessions it holds that no other total counts, over the six token and cost fields only -- it carries no untaggedCostUsd, so untagged spend is outside it, except a claude -p child's share an untagged descendant turn carries when the ledger also records that child -- and it is a floor whenever anything went uncounted -- unattributed, past the depth cap, unreachable because the ledger could not be read (spawned.ledgerError), lost with a malformed ledger line (spawned.malformedLedgerLines), or left out as a counted descendant's untagged turns (spawned.descendantUntagged, one {child, untaggedInteractions, untaggedCostUsd} per such descendant, counting its subagent sessions' untagged turns too); the walk stops at depth 5, counted from this session's own edges at depth 1 (docs/spec-230-231-232-spawn-tree-gaps.md covers the sessions it walks from below that), reported in the document, and a ledger over 8 MiB is refused outright rather than partly read. spawned.unrecorded[] (#128) lists the sessions -- from harnesses that implement listSpawnCandidates, Claude Code today -- that look like this session's launcher children, that no ledger edge names (when the ledger could not be read, spawned.ledgerError, no edge is known and a recorded child may be listed) and whose cost is not already counted, each with its own cost (null, with skip unreadable, when it cannot be parsed), a tier (named: its cwd contains this session's id, whoever started it; inferred: started by a program, in this repo's checkouts or a temp sandbox under /tmp or $TMPDIR, in the 30 minutes after a command this session ran) and a basis (cwd-names-parent, worktree or tmp) -- a list, never summed into total, spawned.total or tree, and never a cause of exit 9. [] also for a session that ran no command, which has nothing to look near. No ANSI and nothing else on stdout; human prose goes to stderr and the sentences that would otherwise have been stdout are repeated in the object's notices[]. Exit 9 still applies (see Exit codes). Suppresses the rendering flags (--tokens, --no-cost, --no-tokens, --other, --pad, --interval, --limit, --bucket/--cumulative, --emoji, --timezone). Does NOT apply to the commands that run instead of a report: --help/--why/--version, --watch, and --list/--cleanup/--restart/--stop all keep their own output, and -p is still refused with exit 1. With an interactive terminal, --json no longer skips the picker outright: it shows one whenever the population is AMBIGUOUS, drawn to stderr so stdout stays one clean JSON document (#89); exactly one -s match still selects immediately with no picker, and so does exactly one session discovered with no -s when there is a terminal. With no interactive terminal, wtft selects only through -s: otherwise exit 10 (see Exit codes), naming every match on stderr and nothing on stdout -- this replaces the old auto-pick-the-newest behaviour and its auto-selected-session notice. CLI only. See docs/spec-26-json.md.

Hide the incremental-cost and total-cost columns. Does not change the bar. --cost still chooses a cost bar. On the Pi widget the hide lasts for the rest of the process. Passing the flag again keeps them hidden. The CLI hides for that run only.

Hide the incremental-token and total-token columns. Does not change the bar. --tokens still chooses a token bar. On the Pi widget the hide lasts for the rest of the process. Passing the flag again keeps them hidden. The CLI hides for that run only.

--tokens draws the bar in tokens and prints a per-model token summary table; -C/--cost draws it in $. CLI: the bar is $ when --cost is given anywhere, else tokens when --tokens is, else the wtft config's tokens setting; the summary prints, under the chart, when --tokens comes after any --cost. Pi widget: the later of the two wins and is saved as the config's tokens setting, which also sets the CLI's default bar; --tokens then shows the summary and ignores -i, -l, -b/-c, --tz, -w, -p and -H given with it, while --cost goes on to apply them. The summary has utilization; below TOTAL, a SPAWNED/TREE block for the descendants the spawn ledger records (#116), shown when the walk finds an edge (this session's, or one from a session already inside its total) or the ledger could not be read cleanly, with, when there is at least one, a line counting the descendants whose untagged turns are left out of their edge totals, and their summed untagged cost (#180); before SPAWNED, in the CLI only, a SUBAGENTS block with one row per built-in subagent (its .meta.json description, model and the cost TOTAL already holds for it -- INSIDE TOTAL, never added to it); after SPAWNED, in the CLI only, an UNRECORDED block listing the sessions no spawn record names and no total already counts (#128) -- a named row each ((unreadable) in place of a cost it could not read), and one line per basis for the inferred rows with their count, the readable rows' summed cost ((unreadable) when none is readable) and unreadable count -- NOT in TOTAL or TREE, shown when there is at least one; and, in the CLI only and printed before SPAWNED, when the session or any of its subagent transcripts contains them, an UNCOUNTED line naming compactions and away-recaps (the same counts --json reports as `uncounted`): calls the harness bills for but writes no usage record for, so they are deliberately NOT in TOTAL (#149).

Alias of --tokens, the same in every respect: the bar counts tokens, still split by category, and the per-model token and cost table is printed. Unpriced models (no registry entry and no legacy rate branch) are marked '?', and a legend names, per model, the fallback wtft would price it with. Extend the registry without a rebuild via ~/.config/wtft/pricing.json; a running log parser daemon keeps the rates it started with until wtft-daemon --restart.
Pad output with N spaces on each side (default: 1, max: floor(term/2)-1). The default makes CLI output width match the Pi widget. CLI only; the Pi widget ignores it.
Display this help information.
Display this tool's version.
Explain why you'd run this tool, with user scenarios and anti-use-cases.

CLI only: /wtft has no spawn-record, and refuses the word. SUBCOMMAND, not a report (#116), and POSITIONAL -- it must be the first argument, so `wtft --json spawn-record ...` is refused (exit 2) rather than recorded. Record one parent->child spawn edge in the append-only spawn ledger at $XDG_STATE_HOME/wtft/spawns.jsonl (~/.local/state/wtft/spawns.jsonl by default). A launcher-spawned session -- a pr-review lens, a `herdr agent start` child -- leaves NO trace of its parent in either session file -- unless its launcher put the parent's id in the child's cwd, which the named tier of spawned.unrecorded[] reads -- so there is nothing for a later parse to re-derive; the spawner writes the edge down at spawn time, when it is free, and `claude --session-id <uuid>` means the child's id is known before the child runs. --flag value and --flag=value both work. --json echoes the exact line written; without it nothing is printed. There is no --ts: the clock fills it, so the ledger cannot disagree with itself. Every text field is capped at 512 bytes and the whole line at 4 KiB, which is what keeps one record one write(2). Exits 2 on a missing or unknown flag, a flag with no value, a malformed session id, or an oversized field; 3 when the ledger cannot be written; 0 on a successful append and on --help. A spawner is expected to ignore a failure: the child is then outside the tree, and appears only in spawned.unrecorded[] if it matches a tier there. wtft --json then reports the lineage under `spawned`, with `tree` as self + resolved descendants; `total` keeps meaning this session's own turns.

examples.desc: Show the session's cost chart in a widget below the editor, sized to the terminal, at most 240 columns.
Group by turn count instead of clock time — bin every 5 interactions regardless of how long they took.
Render the bin date/time labels in US Eastern time.
Show up to the last 20 four-hour bins; the widget shows as many as fit its 10 lines.
Show or refresh the cost audit widget, as a plain /wtft does.
View a full, scrollable cost audit timeline inside a fullscreen TUI pager.
Print a histogram of 'Other' commands grouped by semantic sub-category.
Hide the cost audit widget until the next /wtft that draws it, or a new Pi session.
Switch the widget's bar to tokens and print a per-model token summary table to cross-reference costs with /usage.
Watch a session file in real-time and re-render the bar chart as new interactions arrive (CLI only).
Render with zero padding (full terminal width). Default --pad 1 matches Pi widget width (CLI only).
Read this session's exact cost from the machine-readable summary (CLI only).

exitCodes.meaning: Report produced — including when there is nothing to report yet (session file not written, or a tag with no classified data). Under --json the report is one JSON object on stdout; the commands that run instead of a report (--help/--why/--version, and spawn-record on a successful append or --help) also exit 0 and print their own output. --list/--cleanup/--restart/--stop print wtft-daemon's output and exit with its code: 0 when it succeeded, 1 when --stop could not drop a session (its daemon refused the signal, or a harness session's lease changed or could not be removed), when --restart met a holder that refused the signal or outlived SIGKILL, or a respawn that neither ran nor handed off, or when wtft-daemon could not be run (within 10 s, unless the call includes --restart).

Error: no session found or selected, an invalid path, a daemon that could not be spawned or that died before producing data, a refused flag (-p), --stop unable to drop a session, -F unable to rebuild (a daemon that did not stop, a holder that could not be verified as a daemon, a lease another daemon claimed meanwhile, a lease that could not be read, a rebuild lease that could not be written, a daemon that could not be signalled, a lease or tag file that could not be deleted, a daemon that could not be started, or a harness that did not take the session up within 10 s), --list/--cleanup/--restart/--stop unable to run wtft-daemon (within 10 s, unless the call includes --restart), a harness's session tree (Claude Code's projects directory today), or a directory in it, that could not be read while --json or --tokens lists unrecorded spawns, or an unhandled exception. Reason on stderr; under --json stdout carries nothing.

The call was wrong; stdout carries nothing. Any call but spawn-record: an unknown flag, a bare word, a flag with no value (wtft --stop, wtft --stop --json), or a value a flag cannot use (--limit abc, -i 9x, --harness bogus); stderr says why. It is checked before anything the call asks for, so a refused call exits 2 even with --help, --json or -p in it. `wtft spawn-record` (#116): a missing required flag, an unknown flag, a flag with no value, a malformed session id, or an oversized field; nothing was appended.

`wtft spawn-record` only (#116): the record was valid but the ledger could not be written -- an unwritable state dir, or a full disk. The edge is NOT recorded, so the child is invisible to the tree, not `unattributed` (which means an edge we have whose child we could not read). Any partial line left behind is reported as a counted malformed line on the next read; nothing tries to repair it.

Provisional (duppypro/princess-pi-tools#443): the report was produced in full, but a number in it may still change. Under --json, provisional.provisional is true and provisional.reason names the condition, so $? and the field always agree. Two conditions are mode-dependent: subagent-unreadable is found by the uncounted scan, which a plain wtft run that renders bins skips, so a session provisional for that reason alone exits 9 in the modes that scan and 0 on that plain run (docs/spec-26-json.md, Exit codes). descendant-live (a counted descendant is still writing its transcript or one of its subagent transcripts, #133; that edge carries spawned.edges[].live: true) is set only by --tokens and --json, the runs that read the spawn tree.

Session not specified precisely enough (#89): no interactive terminal, and either -s <substring> matched zero or several sessions, or no -s was given at all -- even when the picker's default scope (this worktree, last 20 minutes) holds exactly one session, since that answer would depend on the clock. Zero is included, replacing the old exit 1 'no session found' for this no -s, no-TTY case. Every match is named on stderr; under --json, stdout carries nothing, same as exit 1.

The interactive session selector was cancelled with q or Ctrl-C. SIGINT convention (128+2), not a wtft-specific code. With no interactive terminal wtft never shows the selector at all (see exit 10), so this exit is unreachable there.
